name: Mexico
genZNote: Mexico City is literally sinking — built on a drained Aztec lakebed, parts of it sink up to 40cm a year — while above ground the country still runs on a living blend of Aztec and Mayan heritage layered under Spanish colonial architecture.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in North America, bordered by the United States to the north and Belize and Guatemala to the south, with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and Gulf of Mexico.
Diverse terrain including central highland plateaus, the Sierra Madre mountain ranges, tropical southern rainforests, and northern deserts.
Mexico City, built atop the drained ancient Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan's lakebed, is one of the world's largest and most populous metropolitan areas.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Spanish is the dominant language, though Mexico has no single official national language and recognises over 60 indigenous languages, reflecting deep pre-Columbian heritage.
Home to major ancient civilizations including the Aztec and Maya, whose pyramids, calendars, and cultural traditions remain deeply woven into national identity.
Globally influential cuisine (recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage), vibrant traditions like Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead), and mariachi music.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal presidential republic composed of 31 states and Mexico City (a federal entity), modelled significantly on the US constitutional structure.
Gained independence from Spain in 1821 after a prolonged war, following nearly three centuries of Spanish colonial rule.
The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) dominated Mexican politics for over 70 years (1929-2000) before the country transitioned to genuine multi-party democratic competition.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant global pharmaceutical manufacturing base and growing medical tourism destination, particularly for dental and cosmetic care from the US.
Strong automotive and aerospace manufacturing sectors integrated closely with US and Canadian supply chains (USMCA).
Ancient Mesoamerican civilizations made notable advances in astronomy, mathematics (including an early concept of zero), and calendar systems.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A G20 member and a key partner in the USMCA (US-Mexico-Canada Agreement), deeply integrated with the North American economy.
Manages a complex, high-volume relationship with the United States around trade, migration, and border security.
An active member of the OECD and a significant voice in Latin American regional diplomacy.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Mexico maintain a 'Privileged Partnership', with growing trade in pharmaceuticals, automobiles, and information technology services.
Mexico is an important gateway for Indian companies seeking access to North American markets via the USMCA framework.
Growing cultural and educational exchange, alongside cooperation in renewable energy and space research.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A major manufacturing hub tightly integrated with the US and Canadian economies through USMCA, especially in automobiles and electronics ('maquiladora' export manufacturing).
One of the world's largest producers of silver, alongside significant oil production and agricultural exports (avocados, tequila).
A major global tourism destination, particularly along its Caribbean and Pacific coastlines (e.g., Cancún).

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Ancient Aztec and Maya civilizations and their pyramids and calendars.
Globally influential cuisine and traditions like Día de los Muertos.
Being one of the world's largest silver producers.
Deep manufacturing integration with the US and Canada through USMCA.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Mexican Peso (MXN).
One of the largest economies in Latin America, with strong manufacturing (automotive, electronics) closely tied to trade with the US and Canada under the USMCA agreement.
A major exporter of vehicles, electronics, and crude oil.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Ranks among the world's most biodiverse countries.
Hosts UNESCO-protected monarch butterfly overwintering sites in its central highlands.
Ecosystems range from northern deserts to tropical rainforest in the south.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Home to ancient Mesoamerican civilizations, including the Maya and Aztec.
Conquered by Spain in the 16th century; achieved independence in 1821 after a decade-long war.
The Mexican Revolution (1910-1920) reshaped the modern state and its political institutions.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1821 independence from Spain ended three centuries of colonial rule.
The 1917 Constitution, born from the Mexican Revolution, remains in force and was notably progressive for its era, including labor and land-reform provisions.
A federal presidential republic.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Agencia Espacial Mexicana (AEM) supports satellite and space-research initiatives.
A growing aerospace-manufacturing sector supplies global supply chains, particularly for North America.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is the most popular sport nationwide.
Home to a rich muralist art tradition, including Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo.
Chichén Itzá and Teotihuacán are major UNESCO World Heritage archaeological sites; Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) is UNESCO-recognised Intangible Cultural Heritage.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN, G20, and OECD.
Part of the USMCA trade agreement with the United States and Canada; a founding member of the Pacific Alliance.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Mexico is a North American federal presidential republic with deep Aztec and Maya heritage, tightly integrated with the US and Canadian economies through USMCA.
keyFacts: Capital: Mexico City. Currency: Mexican Peso.
Federal presidential republic; 31 states plus Mexico City.
Independent from Spain since 1821; PRI dominated politics 1929-2000.
World's largest silver producer; deeply integrated into USMCA manufacturing.
commonConfusion: Mexico has no single constitutionally designated official language — Spanish is dominant in practice, but over 60 indigenous languages are also legally recognised.

highYieldFacts: Mexico: federal presidential republic, capital Mexico City, independent since 1821.
World's largest silver producer; core USMCA manufacturing partner with the US and Canada.
India-Mexico: Privileged Partnership; Mexico serves as an India gateway to North American markets.
commonTraps: Assuming Spanish is Mexico's sole official language by law — it has no single official language, though Spanish dominates.
Confusing modern Mexico's political history (independence 1821, PRI era 1929-2000) with its much older Aztec/Maya civilizational history.
mustRemember: Mexico: Aztec/Maya heritage, federal republic since 1821, USMCA manufacturing hub, top silver producer, growing India trade gateway.
